glossary.Thyroid hormone: T4 and T3, made by the thyroid, which set the body's metabolic rate.
glossary.Metabolism: The chemical processes that use energy in the body's cells.
glossary.Iodine deficiency: Too little dietary iodine, which the thyroid needs to make hormone.
glossary.Autoimmune: The immune system attacking the body's own tissue.
glossary.Post-thyroiditis: Hypothyroidism following thyroid inflammation, such as after viral or postpartum thyroiditis.
glossary.Cold intolerance: Feeling cold easily when others are comfortable.
glossary.Heavy menstrual periods: Excess menstrual blood loss, also called menorrhagia.
glossary.Hoarse voice: A rough, croaky voice, here from tissue swelling of the vocal cords.
glossary.Periorbital puffiness: Swelling of the soft tissue around the eyes.
glossary.Coeliac disease: Autoimmune reaction to gluten that damages the small bowel lining.
glossary.HLA-DR5: An immune gene variant linked to Hashimoto's.
glossary.SLE: Systemic lupus erythematosus, a multi-system autoimmune disease.
glossary.Graves' disease: Autoimmune hyperthyroidism from antibodies that stimulate the TSH receptor.
glossary.Addison's disease: Autoimmune destruction of the adrenal cortex, causing cortisol and aldosterone deficiency.
glossary.Primary hypothyroidism: Hypothyroidism caused by failure of the thyroid gland itself, so TSH is high.
glossary.Half-life: The time for the level of a substance in the body to halve.
glossary.Adherence: How well a patient takes a medicine as prescribed.
glossary.Osteoporosis: Thin, weak bones that fracture easily.
glossary.Angina: Chest pain from heart muscle not getting enough oxygen.
glossary.Calcium carbonate: A calcium supplement and antacid that reduces levothyroxine absorption.
glossary.Digoxin: A heart drug for AF and heart failure that interacts with levothyroxine.
glossary.HRT: Hormone replacement therapy with oestrogen in menopause.
glossary.Iron deficiency anaemia: Low haemoglobin with small red cells from lack of iron.
glossary.mU/L: Milliunits per litre, the unit for TSH.
glossary.Watch-and-wait: Monitoring without treatment, starting only if things change.
glossary.Basal metabolic rate: Energy the body uses at rest.
glossary.Follicular cell: The thyroid cell that makes thyroid hormone.
glossary.Contractility: How strongly the heart muscle contracts.
glossary.Gut motility: Movement of food along the gut by muscle contraction.
glossary.Decompensated: When the body can no longer cope with a disease and organs start to fail.
glossary.Respiratory failure: The lungs cannot keep blood oxygen or carbon dioxide in the normal range.
glossary.GCS: Glasgow Coma Scale, scoring consciousness from 3 to 15.
